s5.forces.gravity.prompt: What force pulls unsupported objects towards Earth?
s5.forces.gravity.hint: It keeps your feet on the ground.
s5.forces.gravity.explain: Gravity attracts objects towards the Earth.

choices: the force of gravity acting on an object
the amount of space an object takes
s5.forces.gravity.answer: the force of gravity acting on an object
s5.forces.gravity.hint: Weight can change on another planet.
s5.forces.gravity.explain: Weight is the force of gravity acting on an object's mass.

s5.forces.gravity.prompt: What usually happens to an object as it falls?
choices: gravity pulls it towards the ground
s5.forces.gravity.answer: gravity pulls it towards the ground
s5.forces.gravity.hint: Think about the direction of the fall.
s5.forces.gravity.explain: Gravity pulls falling objects towards the centre of the Earth.

s5.forces.gravity.prompt: Which force can slow a falling object through air?
s5.forces.gravity.explain: Air resistance acts against motion through the air.

s5.space.earth.hint: It is the star at the centre of our solar system.
s5.space.earth.explain: Earth travels around the Sun in an orbit.

choices: the Sun going around Earth each day
the Moon blocking the Sun every night
s5.space.earth.hint: One side faces the Sun while the other faces away.
s5.space.earth.explain: As Earth rotates, different parts face the Sun and experience day or night.

choices: a planet with its own Sun
s5.space.earth.explain: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.

s5.space.earth.prompt: How long does Earth take to orbit the Sun?
s5.space.earth.hint: It gives us a year and the seasons.
s5.space.earth.explain: Earth completes one orbit of the Sun in about 365 days.

s5.materials.changes.hint: The material can become solid again.
s5.materials.changes.explain: Melted ice can freeze back into water ice, so the change is reversible.

s5.materials.changes.prompt: Which change makes a new material?
s5.materials.changes.hint: The ash and gases are different materials.
s5.materials.changes.explain: Burning is an irreversible change that produces new materials.

s5.materials.changes.prompt: What happens when salt dissolves in water?
choices: the salt spreads through the water and can be recovered by evaporation
the salt turns into a new metal
s5.materials.changes.answer: the salt spreads through the water and can be recovered by evaporation
s5.materials.changes.hint: Dissolving is not the same as destroying.
s5.materials.changes.explain: The salt forms a solution and can be recovered when the water evaporates.

s5.materials.changes.prompt: Which is evidence that a new material may have formed?
choices: a gas or new colour appears during a reaction
s5.materials.changes.answer: a gas or new colour appears during a reaction
s5.materials.changes.explain: Bubbles, a new colour or a temperature change can show that new materials formed.
